description: WeBus is a web-based simulation tool for planning the electrification of transit bus fleets, built jointly by Berliner Verkehrsbetriebe, the Technical University of Berlin and the Reiner Lemoine Institute. The announcement read on 2026-09-29 says it lets agencies compare battery capacities, charging concepts and charging infrastructure at depots and terminal stops, and shows the effect on vehicle demand, energy consumption and costs. It was launched on 18 August 2026 and is described as a freely available open-source tool aimed at municipalities and small to medium transit companies that lack planning resources, with funding of about 1.26 million euro from the German Federal Ministry of Transport. It runs as a hosted web application at the RLI address, so no installation is needed. Coverage is generic to bus networks, not tied to one city, although the partners are in Germany. Caveats: the page does not name the licence or repository, gives no model documentation and the tool is new, so validation is unknown. It suits capacity planning and charging optimisation for public transport electrification.
